incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: p99 latency > SLO on dedicated pool eu-west-1-dedicated-3. Started 08:12 UTC. Affected: streaming/generation paths (tail stalls). Paging oncall @Monica :rotating_light:
Monica: on it. which customers impacted? p95/p99 numbers? any streaming stall traces?
Sam: digging in telemetry now. p95 ~= 340ms (ok), p99 ~= 3.2s (spike). Streaming stall count spiked ~08:11-08:18 UTC. Queue depth for pool = 420 requests, handshake-warmup pending = 34 slots, prewarmed instances = 2, target autoscale pool size = 24, current heated slots = 16. GPU util ~92% on a few nodes.
Priya: sounds like dedicated capacity saturation + autoscaler warmup lag. warmup handshakes showing timeouts in logs -> clients sit in queue until KV cache/weights ready -> streaming stalls.
Sam: past 1h scaling events for that pool:
```
rictl pool events --pool eu-west-1-dedicated-3 --since 1h
2023-08-xxT07:55: scale_up requested -> 4 nodes
2023-08-xxT08:05: scale_up requested -> 8 nodes
2023-08-xxT08:10: scale_up handshake delayed (warmup 45s avg) -> partial accept
2023-08-xxT08:12: burst arrival + queued requests 420
2023-08-xxT08:15: manual scale attempt failed (cold image pull timeout)
```
Sam: logs show repeated `handshake: warmup_slot_not_ready` and `checkpoint load slow` from two hosts (10.8.4.21, 10.8.4.22).
Monica: ok. triage plan? we need quick mitigation (reduce customer impact) + long-term fix.
Priya: immediate mitigations (fast, low-risk):
- enable emergency burst reserve for this pool (adds prewarmed slots)
- shift non-critical traffic to fallback model (lower-memory variant)
- temporarily increase handshake timeout threshold so partial streams don't abort (preserve user-facing streaming)
- open internal ticket for image-pull timeout on the two hosts
Sam: running commands now: `rictl pool set --name eu-west-1-dedicated-3 --reserve-burst 8` and `rictl route update --tag best-effort --pool eu-west-1-dedicated-3 --weight -30` (reduce load).
```
# stdout (sanitized)
> rictl pool set --reserve-burst 8
OK: reserve burst increased from 0 -> 8 (effective within 20s)
> rictl route update ...
OK: route weights updated; best-effort traffic will be diverted
```
Chris: I alerted support and opened INC-19785 for customers with active sessions. Slack thread -> #support-ops. I posted a short customer-facing blurb we can reuse: "We're observing elevated latency on some dedicated pools, engineering is mitigating; minimal data impact; we'll follow up."
Aisha: I'm on infra host cleanup. I'm seeing docker image registry slow push in eu-west. Kicking off a manual pre-pull on affected hosts: `ssh build-ops@10.8.4.21 sudo ri-agent prepull --image model-v2-quant --timeout 120`
Priya: also flipping autoscaler cooldown to be more aggressive for bursts: `rictl autoscaler set --pool eu-west-1-dedicated-3 --burst-cooldown 15s --max-burst 12` (temporary).
Monica: noted. Who owns the postmortem? we need RCA owner and a page to eng-runtime if image pulls are flaky.
Sam: I'll grab RCA for runtime warmup path + scheduling. Priya to lead autoscaler tuning & SLO guardrails. Aisha to follow up with infra registry team. Chris to collect customer impact (which accounts saw > 2s p99).
Priya: quick check: are any other pools showing same pattern? Sam: scanning... eu-west-1-dedicated-2 has minor uptick but within SLO. This one had an unusual concurrent burst (customer onboarding flow + scheduled background jobs).
Monica: good. execute customer mitigation plan: Chris please post updates in #support-ops and ping affected customers (use INC-19785). Keep copy of the blurb.
Chris: done. message sent to top 6 accounts, posted in ticket.
Sam: monitoring: reserve-burst took effect ~08:18 UTC. queue depth dropping from 420 -> 120 over 4m. p99 trending down to 890ms at 08:21. Streaming stalls count decreasing.
incident-bot: STATUS UPDATE: p99 reduced to 890ms. still above target but improving.
Monica: keep observing. Priya, any quick config to avoid handshake timeouts while we fix images?
Priya: setting `handshake_retry=3` and `handshake_timeout=60s` on the pool to allow retries. Command: `rictl pool set --name eu-west-1-dedicated-3 --handshake-retry 3 --handshake-timeout 60`
Sam: applied. logs now show fewer `handshake abort` lines.
Aisha: pre-pull completed on 10.8.4.21 and 10.8.4.22, images ready. I'll cycle agents on those hosts in a staggered manner (no full drain).
Monica: once hosts are stable, start rolling back emergency settings (reserve-burst + handshake-timeout) to normal to avoid cost drift. Who will handle rollback?
Priya: I'll plan rollback in 2h after confirm steady-state. Monica: agreed. assign follow-ups:
- Sam: RCA writeup (runtime warmup latency) -> due EOD
- Priya: autoscaler param changes + rollback plan -> due +2h
- Aisha: registry ticket & host remediation details -> due +4h
- Chris: customer notification & impact summary -> due +1h
Monica: updating incident channel with runbook links: https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/dedicated-warmup-handoff and paging playbook.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: p99 returned to baseline (p99 ~ 210ms) at 08:31 UTC. Incident duration ~19m. tagging as Priority: P2.
Monica: thanks everyone. I'll create the postmortem doc and ping eng-runtime + infra for a follow-up sync tomorrow. If anyone has notes, drop them in the doc (INC-19785-postmortem).
Sam: note for postmortem: consider adding prewarm image pre-pull as part of warmup pipeline and improve autoscaler probe to detect slow registry pulls.
Priya: note: add autoscaler fast-path for short high-concurrency bursts (avoid full cold start when traffic pattern is brief).
Chris: customer impact summary: 6 accounts saw degraded streaming experience, none reported errors, two reported interrupted sessions which were retried client-side. Support closed 4 of 6 with workaround info.
Aisha: infra: registry team repro'd slow push from mirror, they redeployed mirror node and will monitor. ticket INF-5021 opened.
Monica: closing thread for now. Will link postmortem here when ready. :white_check_mark:
